rationale: A narrative review suits a lay committee and a heterogeneous, mostly vignette-based evidence base where pooling would mislead. It should present vignette results (c1) separately from the single real-user comparison (c2), explain why vignettes overstate accuracy (c3), and ground its advice to the committee in what the companies must show.
alternatives: Systematic review with meta-analysis (refused: heterogeneous vignette methods, version drift and 80 hours)
Commissioned real-user evaluation of both apps (refused for now: beyond the time and budget before February; recommended to the committee as a condition)
whyNotMoreComplex: A pooled accuracy figure across vignette studies and app versions would look precise and describe no app the committee would list.

decision.statement: Write a narrative review for the committee that reports vignette and real-user evidence separately, states that no retrieved study supports listing an app without version-specific real-user data, and lists what the two companies should be asked to show.
decision.question: What review should the committee receive before deciding on listing the two apps?

criteria.text: Vignette evidence shows moderate and variable accuracy and real-user evidence shows under-triage of some emergencies.
Vignette studies can be distinguished from real-user studies in the reporting.

gates.requirement: Committee request and deadline for the review
gates.evidence: Committee minute DHC-2026-31 of 2026-09-08, supplied by the investigator
Librarian email of 2026-09-15 confirming 12 hours in October 2026, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Commissioned real-user evaluation of both apps as a listing condition
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; replaces the earlier proposal that rested on a claim not in the ledger.

summary: Narrative review recommended on three ledger claims; both gates met on the investigator's facts.
